hero.eyebrow: A blue lodge in Farmington, Michigan
hero.heading: Good men, made better.
hero.text: We are neighbors from many backgrounds and faiths who meet to improve ourselves, support one another, and serve our community.

truths.title: Not a religion
truths.text: Masons come from many faiths. We ask only that a man believe in a Supreme Being, as his own faith understands it. Religion is not debated in lodge.

truths.title: Not political
truths.text: Partisan politics stay outside the lodge room. Members hold every kind of view and meet as equals.

truths.title: Not a secret society
truths.text: Our ceremonies are private, but our members, our meeting place and our principles are public. You’re reading about them now.

eligibility.text: A man at least 18 years old
Who believes in a Supreme Being
Who comes of his own free will, not because someone talked him into it

community.title: Founders Festival
community.text: You’ll find us at Farmington’s summer festival every year.

community.title: Child ID Program
community.text: Free identification kits for local families.

community.title: Scholarships
community.text: We support students from our community as they head to college.

community.title: Fellowship
community.text: Picnics, dinners and movie nights, often with families along.

faq.question: Is Freemasonry a cult?
faq.answer: No. Members are free to leave at any time, we don’t recruit, and no one is asked to give up his faith, family or independent judgment. Masonry asks a man to be a better version of who he already is.

faq.question: What does membership cost?
faq.answer: There is a one-time initiation fee and modest annual dues. We’ll go over it openly before you petition.

faq.question: How much time does it take?
faq.answer: One regular meeting a month, plus degree work while you progress. Beyond that, you take part as much as your life allows.

faq.question: Can I tell my family I’m a Mason?
faq.answer: Yes. Many Masons are proud to say so. What stays private are the ceremonies and modes of recognition, not your membership.

faq.question: Do I need to know a Mason to join?
faq.answer: No. If you don’t know one, contact us and we’ll introduce you to some of the brethren.

visit.label: When
visit.text: Dinner before our monthly meeting. Second Tuesday, 6:00 pm.

visit.label: What to wear
visit.text: Business casual is fine for dinner.

visit.label: Who greets you
visit.text: A member will meet you at the door and sit with you.

visit.label: Getting in
visit.text: Parking on site, including accessible spaces near the entrance.

contact.privacy: Your note goes only to the lodge secretary. We don’t share it or add you to any list.
